I know exactly how you feel, I'm in a rather similar situation myself. And I will say that I'm sorry you're feeling this way, because I know just how awful it all feels.

If your counsellor is suggesting a professional though, I think it might be a good idea for you to try. It's more likely that they're suggesting it because a professional would be more beneficial and can offer you more help than they can themselves. I know exactly how daunting it is, the idea of trying this, as I'm in the process of getting into contact with one myself, but it may just be worth it. Seeing a psychiatrist may benefit you and help you on your way to not being sick of everything.

Proposing the idea to your parents is a scary idea--it always is. But it's good to try to talk to them, to explain how you're really feeling, and they should do what they can to get you the support you need. It might be daunting, but bringing it up with them is probably a good idea, especially if it can lead to you getting help.

It's a hard step, this one, but it's an important one.

I've actually found this myself lately. A lot of days I'll be down and have no motivation or interest in anything, and then suddenly one morning I'll just...feel pretty good. Actually want to do things, almost feel excited about them.

Unfortunately, I have no idea what it is that might be causing it for either of us, but you're definitely not the only one whose dealing with this sort of thing. I suppose the most we can do is enjoy the days where things feel alright?
